extraction.summary: Roy Choudhury updates the H0 Distance Network (H0DN) supernova Hubble-flow rung using two distinct inputs: revised Pantheon+ host-mass bias corrections and DES-DOVEKIE distance moduli. In the main isolated calculation, 52 of 277 H0DN Hubble-flow rows receive only revised apparent magnitudes; H0DN covariance, redshifts and velocity treatment remain fixed, and the 55 calibrator supernovae are unchanged. The reported result shifts from 73.499±0.809 to 73.264±0.806 km s^-1 Mpc^-1. A separate full Pantheon+ replacement uses the public Pantheon+ covariance and redshift/velocity treatment and gives 73.139±0.791; the additional shift is attributed mainly to redshift/flow treatment, since the stated covariance matrices agree. DES-DOVEKIE replaces the Hubble-flow sample with 220 rows, 196 of which overlap corrected Pantheon+. A single weighted magnitude offset fitted on those overlaps gives 73.267±0.828 when held fixed; propagating the available within-release and Pantheon+ covariance through the offset gives 73.175±0.854, while the median-offset check gives 72.991±0.825. The uncertainty-propagation expression omits DES–Pantheon+ cross-covariance because none is public; the overlapping samples therefore are not independent and the full uncertainty remains incompletely known. With q0=-0.55 and j0=1 fixed, raising the Hubble-flow upper redshift to 0.30 raises both samples' fitted H0 rather than moving them toward the stated CMB+flat-LCDM comparison. These are conditional distance-ladder fits and sensitivity checks, not independent measurements, a dust-population test, or a cosmological mechanism. None of the reported updates removes the quoted early–late difference.

ideas.title: Object-level host-mass bias-branch update and H0DN response
ideas.description: The authors reconstruct a corrected Pantheon+ magnitude vector from public inputs, reporting agreement with a privately supplied corrected file to floating-point precision. They fit separate unweighted degree-three polynomials f_low(c_SALT) and f_high(c_SALT) to public biasCor_m_b values over 713 rows with 0.01<=z_CMB<0.15, split by the published log10(M*/M_sun)=10 host-mass step. For 114 rows whose published host masses were 9.4<=log10(M*/M_sun)<10 and are said to be underestimated by about 0.6 dex, they replace the low-branch correction with the high-branch value: Delta_i=f_low(c_i)-f_high(c_i), m_corr_i=m_public_i+Delta_i. This moves 52 H0DN Hubble-flow rows (46 distinct names); none of 55 calibrators changes. They add only the magnitude delta to matching H0DN rows and hold its covariance, redshifts and peculiar-velocity treatment fixed. This is a branch substitution in an existing empirical BBC correction, not a newly fitted constant mass-step amplitude, a rerun of bias simulations, or a test of distinct physical dust populations.
locators: PDF p.4, first results discussion; PDF p.5 Table 1/Figure 1; PDF p.8 Conclusion

equations.definitions: c_SALT is the Pantheon+ light-curve color parameter; i indexes a released row; f_low/high are separate unweighted cubic fits to public biasCor_m_b values on the two host-mass branches.
equations.domain: Fit sample: 713 public Pantheon+ rows, 0.01<=z_CMB<0.15. Updated subset: 114 rows with published host masses 9.4<=log10(M*/M_sun)<10 that cross the log10(M*/M_sun)=10 step after the stated ~0.6 dex revision.

equations.definitions: old/new denote H0DN Hubble-flow magnitudes before/after applying the corrected-minus-public Pantheon+ change.
equations.domain: 52 affected H0DN Hubble-flow rows among 277; 46 distinct supernova names. Calibrator rows are not changed.

equations.definitions: M_B is the calibrated SN Ia absolute magnitude and alpha_B is the Hubble-flow intercept in the H0DN convention.
equations.domain: H0DN local distance-network fit; its non-SN distance indicators and shared calibrations remain part of the network.

ideas.result: H0DN baseline 73.499±0.809 becomes 73.264±0.806 km s^-1 Mpc^-1 (delta -0.235). The 52-row mean correction is 0.06391 mag, but the authors' influence-weighted correction is 0.0085 mag; they state a coherent 0.236 mag Hubble-flow faintening would be required to shift the complete network central value to 67.24. These are reported fit outputs; the input artifacts and fit were not independently rerun.
assumptions_and_limits: Low-z host masses are revised as stated by Hoyt et al.; no host-mass source data were checked here.
The bias-branch correction uncertainty is reported as <0.02 mag and nearly unchanged, so the authors do not update covariance; that covariance decision was not independently audited.
The paper does not rerun the full bias-correction simulations.
A host-mass correction result does not by itself discriminate two-population dust from intrinsic color, selection, calibration or other standardization effects.

ideas.title: Single additive offset transfers DES-DOVEKIE moduli to the H0DN magnitude scale
ideas.description: For DES-DOVEKIE, the authors turn released distance moduli into H0DN-convention apparent magnitudes by estimating one constant offset on the 196 supernovae shared with corrected Pantheon+. The fiducial DES sample has 220 rows in 0.02509<=z_HD<=0.15062 (197 external-survey and 23 DES-observed); 36 overlap rows carry a Pantheon+ host correction. Per-object C_i=m_corr_b,i-mu_DES,i and w_i=1/sigma_mu,i^2 define C_DES=-19.3766 mag. They hold this constant for the fiducial intercept and for redshift extensions. Offset adequacy is motivated by a fitted slope 0.195±0.255 mag per redshift and 0.0823 mag scatter; the constant also absorbs release H0 normalization and any mean difference in light-curve shape/color, host step, bias correction and photometric calibration. Those contributions cannot be separated from the overlap alone.
locators: PDF p.5 Table 1 and Figure 1(b); PDF pp.6-7 Figure 2

equations.definitions: mu_DES is released DES-DOVEKIE distance modulus; sigma_mu,i is its released per-object distance-modulus uncertainty; the authors use inverse-variance scalar weights.
equations.domain: 196 cross-matched supernovae at the fiducial upper cut z_HD,max=0.151; DES release has nominal H0=70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1.

equations.definitions: The fitted additive offset places DES-DOVEKIE moduli on the apparent-magnitude convention of H0DN.
equations.domain: 220 selected DES-DOVEKIE Hubble-flow rows; constant fitted using the 196 overlapping Pantheon+ rows.

equations.expression: y=F d+1 w^T(r-S d)=A d+B r; A=F-1 w^T S; B=1 w^T
equations.definitions: d is the full DES modulus vector; r is corrected Pantheon+ magnitudes for overlap rows; F selects Hubble-flow rows; S selects overlaps; w is normalized offset weights; 1 is a column of ones.
equations.domain: Offset covariance propagation for the selected DES flow sample and its overlap-derived magnitude scale.

equations.definitions: V_D and V_R are public DES-DOVEKIE and Pantheon+ covariance matrices.
equations.domain: The paper says no joint DES–Pantheon+ cross-covariance is public. Cross terms are absent from the displayed expression; this is an unresolved uncertainty source, not evidence that the shared-data covariance is physically zero.

ideas.result: Fixed weighted mean: 73.267±0.828 km s^-1 Mpc^-1. Propagating the available covariance: 73.175±0.854, with sigma(C_DES)=0.02309 mag (DES contribution 0.01739, Pantheon+ 0.01520). Median fixed: 72.991±0.825. The offset scatter is 0.0823 mag, its full range is stated as 0.5323 mag, and its fitted redshift slope is 0.195±0.255 mag per unit redshift. The 0.0823-mag scatter corresponds to about 3.8% in luminosity distance under the stated modulus conversion; it is not an independent sample-level error estimate.
assumptions_and_limits: The fiducial offset is fixed in the first result; that central estimate is conditional on the estimated transfer and its quoted uncertainty is not propagated.

The propagated calculation includes within-DES covariance for measurements reused in the overlap offset, but does not include a joint DES–Pantheon+ cross-covariance; the two products overlap and are explicitly not independent.
The fit uses scalar 1/sigma_mu^2 weights for the offset; the full covariance-based offset estimator and the origin of all released error columns were not independently inspected.
A lack of a resolved linear redshift slope over this low-z overlap does not establish common standardization or rule out host/color/selection-dependent mismatch.

ideas.title: Conditional H0 shifts under nested Hubble-flow redshift cuts
ideas.description: The authors extend corrected Pantheon+ full-rung and DES-DOVEKIE fixed-offset fits through z_HD,max=0.151, 0.20, 0.25 and 0.30, fixing q0=-0.55 and j0=1 throughout. DES uses the overlap offset measured only at 0.151; it is not refitted at higher cuts. The samples are nested, and the reported changes use 5000 joint Gaussian draws retaining covariance between nested cuts. Both sequences rise as higher-redshift SNe are included. This is sensitivity of a data-plus-fixed-cosmography analysis; it does not isolate expansion-history physics from calibration, selection, peculiar-velocity or shared-sample effects.
locators: HTML #S3.SS2; PDF pp.6-7, Figure 2 and surrounding text

equations.expression: Third-order-in-z luminosity-distance relation with fixed (q0,j0)=(-0.55,1); the source describes a quadratic cosmographic correction multiplying leading z but does not display the full expression here.
equations.locator: HTML #S3.SS2; PDF p.6, paragraph preceding the redshift sweep
equations.definitions: The fixed pair matches the authors' flat-Lambda-CDM reference with Omega_m=0.30, Omega_Lambda=0.70. They state the truncated relation differs by about 1 mmag in relative distance modulus over 0.151<=z_HD<=0.30.
equations.domain: Hubble-flow extensions only through z_HD,max=0.30; conclusion is conditioned on fixed deceleration and jerk.

ideas.result: At z_HD,max=0.30, corrected Pantheon+ gives 73.552±0.774 and DES-DOVEKIE 73.995±0.801 km s^-1 Mpc^-1. Relative to 0.151, rises are 0.413±0.179 and 0.728±0.233; their difference is 0.314±0.294, with unavailable cross-covariance omitted. A separate corrected-Pantheon+ lower cut z_HD>0.05 keeps 91/277 rows and gives 72.896±0.858, still quoted 6.11 sigma above the CMB+flat-LCDM reference. The authors also report DES |c_SALT|<0.15 leaves 198 rows and gives 73.338±0.836 with the fixed weighted offset.
assumptions_and_limits: The higher-redshift DES points reuse a zero point calibrated only on the overlapping low-redshift sample.
The inter-compilation cross-covariance for comparing the two redshift trends is omitted; the DES and Pantheon+ samples overlap.
Neither the cut sweep nor the color cut is an independent measurement or a physical test of a redshift-dependent/dust population model.

The source discusses peculiar-velocity uncertainty as sigma_mu,v approximately 5 sigma_v/(ln(10) c z), using sigma_v=240 km/s; this is a low-z uncertainty approximation, not a replacement for the full velocity/covariance lineage.

caveats: The source has one author and reports fits using public inputs, but this worker did not reproduce the results or independently validate the private corrected Pantheon+ file's claimed agreement with reconstructed public data.

The 1-sigma fit uncertainties depend on the H0DN network/calibration model, covariance, fixed q0,j0 convention and (for DES) treatment of the overlap-derived offset. They do not include every unreported or unavailable cross-release systematic.

The DES offset is estimated using 196 objects shared with corrected Pantheon+. Equation (7) carries the available within-release covariance but has no DES-Pantheon+ cross term; the paper says no joint cross-covariance is public. Treating the displayed formula as complete would understate unresolved dependence; the missing term is unknown, not physically zero.

The 196 overlap comparisons include 160 unchanged and 36 host-corrected Pantheon+ rows. A constant offset can absorb mean differences in zero point and reductions, so a small slope over this interval does not prove compatible host/color/dust standardization, selection or calibration.

The reclassified host-mass correction updates an empirical bias-correction branch. It is not a direct two-population dust measurement and does not test whether host-dependent residuals arise from dust versus intrinsic color, selection, or calibration.

The redshift-cut trend is conditional on fixed q0=-0.55,j0=1 and, for DES, a low-z offset frozen at 0.151. Nested samples, overlapping compilations and omitted inter-release covariance prevent interpreting this as an independent expansion-history signal.

The quoted t_CMB statistic is a Gaussian difference using the local-fit and CMB+flat-LCDM error bars in quadrature. The CMB value is model-conditioned; this reading did not check that fit or all systematic covariance assumptions.

usefulness.assessment: Useful as a source-conditional measurement-lineage and sensitivity record: the paper separates a magnitude-only host-mass update from a full Pantheon+ rung replacement and an overlapping DES-DOVEKIE modulus transfer. It exposes that the headline one-sigma values inherit fixed network/cosmography assumptions and incomplete cross-release covariance. It is not a new physical cosmology, an independent H0 confirmation, or a validated dust-population test.
usefulness.minimum_discriminating_checks: A later source review should inspect pinned H0DN input/code and complete calibration covariance; compare the corrected Pantheon+ reconstruction and release files/row joins; verify redshift/velocity roles and duplicate-row lineage; obtain or bound DES-DOVEKIE–Pantheon+ cross-covariance; test the constant offset against redshift, host mass, color, survey/selection strata; and compare an overlap-aware hierarchical standardization against this fixed-offset summary. This is source/dependency work only, not executed here.
usefulness.readiness: needs_review; no executable design proposed. The existing compiled consumer is not established to support hierarchical dust/population calibration, and this source read does not meet numerical, inference or scientific qualification gates.
usefulness.relation_to_existing_register: Relevant to topic measurement-lineage and idea supernova-reduction-selection-dependence. The host correction is a measurement-systematics update and should not be promoted as a distinct dust mechanism without independent source evidence and Sol review. No graph change is made.
